screening_decisions.reason: Retrospective observational study, not an RCT. Examines impact of inappropriate vs appropriate initial therapy, not de-escalation strategy.
Open non-comparative study (not RCT). Wrong population - staphylococcal bone infections, not sepsis/septic shock.
RCT but wrong population - acute pyelonephritis/UTI, not sepsis/septic shock. Compares dosing regimens, not de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Observational study examining cost outcomes, not an RCT. Does not compare de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Clinical practice guidelines document, not an RCT. Consensus recommendations, not primary research.
Cross-sectional observational study describing prescribing patterns, not an RCT. No intervention comparison.
Descriptive epidemiological study using administrative data, not an RCT. No intervention comparison.
Opinion/editorial article, not an RCT. Discusses treatment philosophy without presenting trial data.
Retrospective observational study reviewing de-escalation practices, not an RCT. No randomized comparison of de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Cross-sectional observational study describing antibiotic usage patterns, not an RCT. No intervention comparison.
Review article discussing sepsis management principles, not an RCT. No primary research data.

Multicentre RCT comparing procalcitonin-guided antibiotic strategy vs standard guidelines in ICU patients with suspected bacterial infections. Mortality assessed at 28 and 60 days. While de-escalation is guided by procalcitonin rather than culture results specifically, this represents a de-escalation strategy worth including for full-text review.
Secondary analysis from an RCT examining adequacy of initial empiric therapy, not de-escalation strategy. Does not compare de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Prospective observational study analyzing guideline compliance, not an RCT. No intervention comparison.
Review article discussing optimal antimicrobial therapy principles, not an RCT. No primary research data.
Perspective/opinion article on surgical infection management, not an RCT. No primary research data.
Observational study comparing biomarker levels, not an RCT. No intervention comparison.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis statistics, not an RCT. Completely unrelated to sepsis or antimicrobial therapy.
Review article discussing antibiotic stewardship challenges, not an RCT. No primary research data.
Prospective observational study on biomarkers for diagnosing infected pancreatic necrosis, not an RCT. Wrong population (pancreatitis, not sepsis/septic shock).
Review article about imipenem therapy, not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Review article about streamlining in LRTI, not an RCT; population is LRTI patients, not specifically sepsis/septic shock.
Review article about antibiotic dosing in AKI patients, not an RCT comparing de-escalation strategies.
RCT but in preterm infants (not adults); compares dosing frequency, not de-escalation based on culture results.
Review of patents on carbapenems, not an RCT.
Review article about antibiotic dosing principles, not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.

RCT comparing procalcitonin-guided therapy vs standard care, but intervention is biomarker-guided (not culture-based de-escalation); does not specifically compare de-escalation based on culture results.
Retrospective cohort study, not an RCT; examines timing of therapy and AKI outcomes, not de-escalation strategy.
Implementation study about Surviving Sepsis Campaign, not an RCT comparing de-escalation strategies.
Microbiology study about resistance gene characterization, not an RCT.
Observational study with pharmacist intervention, not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.

RCT but in surgical ICU patients with infections (not specifically sepsis/septic shock); compares PCT-guided duration vs fixed duration, not culture-based de-escalation; primary outcome is duration, not mortality.
Review article about UTIs, not an RCT about sepsis de-escalation.
Retrospective cohort study, not an RCT; examines appropriateness of initial therapy, not de-escalation strategy.
Reporting guidelines for RCTs, not an RCT itself.
Retrospective case record study about meningitis (not sepsis/septic shock), not an RCT.
Review article about empiric therapy selection, not an RCT; explicitly states de-escalation is not necessary.
Letter/comment about a meta-analysis, not an RCT.
Validation study of a severity scoring system, not an RCT about de-escalation.
Guidelines document for antibiotic administration in injured patients, not an RCT about sepsis de-escalation.

RCT but wrong population (ICU patients with pulmonary infiltrates, not specifically sepsis/severe sepsis/septic shock). Intervention uses Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) to guide antibiotic duration, not de-escalation based on culture results.
Retrospective monocentric study, not a randomized controlled trial. Selection criteria require RCTs only.
Review/guideline article providing recommendations on antibiotic strategies, not a randomized controlled trial.
Review article discussing antibiotic therapy management in septic shock, not a randomized controlled trial.
Before-after study design, not an RCT. Focuses on C. difficile outbreak control in elderly care unit, not de-escalation for sepsis/septic shock.
Observational review of blood culture isolates in hemodialysis patients, not a randomized controlled trial.
Review article on Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections, not a randomized controlled trial.
Retrospective review of rapid response system database, not a randomized controlled trial. Evaluates antibiotic algorithm implementation, not de-escalation.
Review article on antibiotic therapy for infectious endocarditis, not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong condition (endocarditis, not sepsis/septic shock).
Review article on severe soft tissue infections management, not a randomized controlled trial.
Review article on sepsis diagnosis and treatment, not a randomized controlled trial.
Commentary on procalcitonin in liver transplant patients, not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong population.

Secondary analysis examining effect of inappropriate vs appropriate initial antimicrobial therapy. Does not test de-escalation intervention. Additionally, explicitly includes patients who received inappropriate (inadequate) initial antimicrobial therapy, which is an exclusion criterion per protocol.
Review article on antibiotic use in neonatal ICU, not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong population (neonates, not adults).
Prospective observational cohort study investigating procalcitonin as mortality predictor, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not test de-escalation intervention.
RCT comparing bolus vs continuous infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam. This tests dosing regimen/pharmacokinetics, not de-escalation based on culture results vs standard therapy.
Review article on antibiotic resistance strategies, not a randomized controlled trial.
Prospective observational epidemiological study of severe sepsis in Chinese ICUs, not a randomized controlled trial. No intervention tested.
Review article on antimicrobial chemotherapy updates, not a randomized controlled trial.
This appears to be the Cochrane review protocol or background document itself (same title as the systematic review), not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a review/opinion article discussing carbapenem use in ICU infections. It is not an RCT and does not compare de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is an observational descriptive study (42 patients over 1 year), not an RCT. The intervention is PCT-guided discontinuation, not de-escalation based on culture results.
This is a retrospective cohort study with no intervention. It examines timing of antimicrobial administration but does not compare de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is a retrospective study in neonates (extremely low birth weight infants), not adults. The review protocol specifies adults with sepsis.
This is a review article discussing antifungal strategies. It is not an RCT and focuses on fungal infections rather than bacterial sepsis de-escalation.
This is an observational study evaluating guideline-concordant therapy for community-acquired pneumonia, not an RCT comparing de-escalation versus standard therapy for sepsis.
This is a prospective observational cohort study describing sepsis incidence and characteristics. It is not an RCT and has no intervention comparison.

This is an observational study comparing ID service vs attending physicians. While it mentions switching from broad to narrow-spectrum agents, it is not an RCT comparing de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is a 1-day point-prevalence observational study. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate de-escalation interventions.
This appears to be a brief statement or editorial summarizing de-escalation benefits. It is not an RCT with comparative data.
This is a review article on UTI diagnosis and management. It is not an RCT and does not focus on sepsis de-escalation.
This is a consensus conference report on sepsis definitions. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate de-escalation interventions.

This is a prospective observational study (not an RCT) evaluating de-escalation in ventilator-associated pneumonia. While it uses culture results to modify therapy, it lacks randomization and control group comparison.
This is a review article discussing sepsis management recommendations. It is not an RCT comparing de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is a methodology paper on clinical measurement validity in cardiology. It is completely unrelated to sepsis or antimicrobial de-escalation.
This is a prospective cohort study in neonates (NICU), not adults. Additionally, it includes patients with inadequate empiric therapy, which is an exclusion criterion per the protocol.

While this is an RCT in adults with severe sepsis, the intervention is PCT-guided discontinuation of antibiotics, not de-escalation based on culture results. The protocol specifically requires de-escalation based on culture results, not biomarker-guided discontinuation.
This is an RCT in critically ill adults, but the intervention is selective decontamination of the digestive tract (SDD), not de-escalation of antimicrobial therapy based on culture results.
This is an observational cross-sectional prevalence study. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate de-escalation interventions.
This is a review article on antibiotic pharmacokinetics and dosing in CRRT patients. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate de-escalation strategies.
Observational cohort study (not RCT) describing sepsis incidence in Brazilian ICUs. No de-escalation intervention.
Pharmaco-epidemiological observational study of antibiotic use patterns in Italian ICUs. Not an RCT.
Prospective surveillance study categorizing antibiotic indications. Observational design, not an RCT.
Randomized trial but includes CHILDREN (3 months-15 years), not adults. Population does not match criteria.
Review/discussion article about wound management and antimicrobial resistance. Not an RCT.
Cluster-randomized trial but focuses on lower respiratory tract infections (not sepsis/septic shock). Intervention is procalcitonin-guided treatment, not de-escalation based on culture results.
Study protocol for NEONATES AND CHILDREN, not adults. Population does not match criteria.
Trend analysis using administrative data (1993-2003). Observational study, not an RCT.
Retrospective descriptive study evaluating blood culture yield. Not an RCT.
Prospective cohort study evaluating adequate empirical antibiotic therapy impact. Not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Review article discussing antibiotic de-escalation concept. Not an RCT with primary data.
Retrospective analysis of medical records from patients with positive blood cultures. Observational study, not an RCT.
Review/discussion article about nosocomial pneumonia and de-escalation strategy. Not an RCT.
Prospective observational study evaluating VAP treatment appropriateness. Not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Review article discussing principles of antibiotic therapy. Not an RCT.
Retrospective cohort study screening blood cultures over 5 years. While examining de-escalation in bacteraemia, it is NOT an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.
